facts.raw_span: 2-month history of diplopia and pain
recurring forehead lesion, first excised 6 years prior to presentation
Breslow thickness of 6 mm
14 mitotic figures/mm2
no ulceration
extensive perineural and intraneural invasion
Visual acuity was 20/20 bilaterally without afferent pupillary defect
left proptosis and resistance to globe retropulsion with edema, erythema, and ptosis of the left upper eyelid
Adduction was limited on the left, with associated strabismus and forehead anesthesia in the V1 division of the trigeminal nerve
Left superior orbit mass extending along the supraorbital nerve to the cavernous sinus, with indistinct borders and fat stranding
Intense enhancement of the V1 branch of the left frontal nerve with associated fat stranding
Cross section of nerve showing malignant cells with mitotic activity, effacing residual nerve axons, disrupted neuronal cells, and peritumoral and intratumoral lymphocytes

The patient has forehead anesthesia in the V1 division of the trigeminal nerve, which is consistent with trigeminal nerve invasion.

The patient has limited adduction on the left with associated strabismus and forehead anesthesia in the V1 division of the trigeminal nerve, which can be seen in optic neuritis.
The patient is in his 60s and has a visual acuity of 20/20 bilaterally, but age-related macular degeneration is a possible diagnosis given his age.
The patient has a history of diplopia and pain, which can be seen in dry eye syndrome.
